why: Normal is paired with only Grass and Ice (16 of 18 combos missing), and Normal/Flying, the classic first-route bird, does not exist. As a three-stage line it grows with the player from the first route to the league.

stages.name: Puffinch
stages.look: A plump, round field-finch chick with cream and tan feathers, a big fluffy chest puff, stubby wings and a long two-strand ribbon tail it trips over. Wide cheerful eyes, little orange feet.

stages.name: Gustling
stages.look: A lean, scrappy young finch that has outgrown its fluff, with a short spiky crest, wings a size too big and the first rust-red feathers coming in at the neck. Its ribbon tail is now long enough to whip.

stages.name: Galeforth
stages.look: A proud, swift hawk with a swept-back windblown crest, tan and white plumage and a rust-red neck ruff that flows like a scarf. Wings half spread, the forked ribbon tail streaming behind it.

dex: It rides the first warm wind of the morning over the fields and never lands until dusk. Riders tie ribbons to its tail for luck before a long journey.

why: Dark and Flying have never been paired, and Psychic/Flying is missing too. Corvlet uses the honor ledger (like Dustcub): a trainer who fights fair raises an oracle, one who fights dirty raises a thief.

stages.name: Corvlet
stages.look: A scruffy crow chick under an oversized hood of black feathers that hides everything but one bright eye. It always carries a stolen shiny trinket in its beak.

stages.name: Ravenmourne
stages.look: A tall, tattered raven wrapped in a cloak of black feathers, its long beak shaped like a plague-doctor mask. A ring of stolen trinkets hangs around its neck and its eyes glint violet.
stages.label: Low honor

stages.name: Augurvane
stages.label: High honor
stages.look: A sleek raven whose black feathers fade to bone-white at the tips, each inscribed with a faint rune. A violet gem glows on its brow like a third eye, and it carries a small lit lantern in its talons.

dex: Every Corvlet steals. What it becomes depends on what it learns from its trainer: the honest ones grow into Augurvanes that return what they took, the rest into Ravenmournes that never give anything back.

why: Bug has only 4 families and no pure Bug at all. A fast-evolving three-stage bug (larva, cocoon, mantis) adds a pure Bug first stage and the missing Bug/Grass combo, the natural forest bug.

stages.name: Sproutgrub
stages.look: A soft green-brown caterpillar curled up in a rolled leaf like a sleeping bag, only its sleepy face and tiny stubby legs poking out. A single sprout grows from its head.

stages.name: Leafcoon
stages.look: A cocoon of tightly wound leaves stitched with silk, hanging from a twig. Two narrow eyes peer out of a gap, and blade-shaped leaf tips already poke through the wrapping, a hint of what is inside.

stages.name: Mantleaf
stages.look: A poised praying mantis whose forearms are serrated leaf blades. A petal crest frames its head and its folded wings carry a moss pattern. Stance low and ready to strike.

dex: It stands so still among the ferns that birds land on it. The leaf on its arm is sharper than any blade a smith could hammer.

why: Ice has only 4 catchable families and has never been paired with Flying. A snowy owl gives Ice a special attacker that does not depend on Water or Dragon.

stages.name: Snowlet
stages.look: A perfectly round snowball of frost fluff with only big amber eyes and a tiny beak showing. Two little wing tips stick out of the sides.

stages.name: Hoarfrowl
stages.look: A large snowy owl whose wing tips are long icicle feathers. A ring of frost circles one eye like a monocle and its breath hangs as fog. Calm, scholarly stare.

dex: A single beat of its wings frosts a whole valley overnight. Climbers on Skyrend say it watches every rope team and only leaves once they are safe.

why: Pure Ice does not exist yet and Ice/Ground is missing. The calf is pure Ice and picks up Ground when it evolves, a type change across stages the roster rarely uses. It gives Ice the physical tank it lacks.

stages.name: Tuskling
stages.look: A woolly calf with shaggy brown fur, a cap of fresh snow on its head and two tiny frosted tusk nubs. Short sturdy legs and a curious, trunk-up pose.

stages.name: Shagtusk
stages.look: A stocky young mammoth with a thick shaggy coat caked in frozen mud, short straight tusks capped in ice and a stubborn lowered head, ready to charge. Thin sheets of frost are forming along its spine.

stages.name: Rimetusk
stages.look: A towering mammoth with slabs of permafrost grown onto its back like a small glacier, huge curled tusks rimmed with ice and frozen clods of earth tangled in its fur.

dex: Herds migrate along the same path every winter and leave a road of packed ice behind them. The glacier on an old bull's back is older than any town on the mountain.

why: Poison and Ground each sit at 6 families and have never been combined. A desert scorpion is a natural fit and gives Poison a sturdy physical line.

stages.name: Scorpit
stages.look: A tiny sand-coloured scorpion with a stinger far too big for its body that it drags behind it. Little pincers held up proudly.

stages.name: Dunevenom
stages.look: An armoured desert scorpion whose plates are layered like sandstone strata. Its venom bulb glows purple and drips onto the sand, and its pincers are wide as shovels.

dex: It burrows under the dunes and leaves a faint purple trail that kills every weed it crosses. Miners in Marrowdig shake out their boots twice.

why: Rock has 6 families and has never been paired with Flying. A revived fossil pterosaur is a strong fantasy and can be a dig-site gift, so it needs no spawn zone.

stages.name: Shalewing
stages.look: A hatchling pterosaur still half inside a cracked shale egg, wearing the top half of the shell like a helmet. Thin membrane wings and a big curious beak.

stages.name: Petraptor
stages.look: A large pterosaur whose wings are layered slate plates, with ridges of fossil bone along its back and a polished amber gem set into its long crest.

dex: It ruled the skies before the mountains were this tall. The amber in its crest still holds a mosquito from that age.

why: Cosmic is almost legendary-only: one catchable family (Hollowolf) and no pure Cosmic. Two pure Cosmic stages, then Fairy at the last stage, make Cosmic a type a player can raise from the start.

stages.name: Twinklit
stages.look: A small five-pointed star creature with a sleepy smiling face and stubby star-point limbs, trailing a thin line of glitter wherever it floats.

stages.name: Lumistar
stages.look: A small floating star child: its head is a soft five-pointed star with a calm glowing face, and below it hangs a short little body wrapped in a cape of deep night sky dotted with tiny stars. Two small mitten hands, no legs, it floats above a short comet trail. A faint ring of light circles its head like a halo.

stages.name: Stellaria
stages.look: A graceful floating dancer whose flowing gown is a nebula veil dotted with a constellation. A crown of small stars circles its head and its feet never touch the ground.

dex: Astronomers at the Umbral Observatory have charted one new constellation for every Stellaria they have met. It dances them into the sky and they stay there.

why: A second catchable Cosmic family, built as the physical counterpart to Stellaria. Cosmic/Rock is missing and makes Cosmic feel like a real type outside the legendaries.

stages.name: Meteorb
stages.look: A small cratered meteorite that hovers a little off the ground, a teal glow leaking from the cracks in its surface and two pebble eyes peering out.

stages.name: Craterhulk
stages.look: A hulking golem of meteor rock. Its chest is a crater with a glowing star core inside, its knuckles still glow red-hot from entry, and small debris orbits its shoulders.

dex: The crater on Skyrend is where the first one landed. It climbed out, looked at the stars and has been trying to punch its way back ever since.

why: There is no pure Ghost and Ghost has never met Ground. A desert grave spirit fits the badlands zones and gives Ghost a defensive line.

stages.name: Gravelwisp
stages.look: A little wisp wrapped in a loose burial cloth, two glowing eyes in the dark under the hood and a thin stream of sand trickling from its hem as it drifts.

stages.name: Tombdune
stages.look: A walking sandstone sarcophagus. The lid is cracked open and a sand-ghost spills out of it, with glowing eyes behind a carved mask and arms of pouring sand.

dex: It guards a tomb that no map shows. Anyone who digs near it hears sand pouring, even when the air is perfectly still.

why: Water/Dark, the classic shark, is missing. Dark has 11 missing combos and this gives Saltmourn's coast a mean, fast physical threat.

stages.name: Gnashfin
stages.look: A shark pup with a jaw much too big for its head, a scar across one eye and fins as ragged as torn sails. Always grinning.

stages.name: Dreadmaw
stages.look: A big pirate-themed shark with ink-black hide, a jagged dorsal fin like a broken hull plank and a rusted anchor chain wrapped around its tail. Rows of white teeth in a wide grin.

dex: Sailors out of Saltmourn count the chains on a Dreadmaw's tail: one for every ship that tried to drag it in. None of them came home with it.

why: Fire and Bug have never been paired. A flame moth is a classic fantasy and gives Bug its second new family in this set.

stages.name: Kindlegrub
stages.look: A soot-black grub with glowing ember stripes between its segments, carrying a smouldering coal on its back like a backpack.

stages.name: Pyremoth
stages.look: A moth whose wings are living flame with eye-spots like glowing embers. Its body is fuzzy and ash-grey, and it sheds a drift of glowing scales as it flies.

dex: Swarms gather over Cinderhold's forges on cold nights. The townsfolk leave the furnace doors open for them, and the town has never once frozen.

why: Normal has only 3 catchable families. A boxing kangaroo is instantly readable, adds Normal/Fighting and suits Forgewall's arena culture.

stages.name: Joeyjab
stages.look: A young kangaroo with oversized red boxing-glove paws and a sweatband on its head, bouncing on its toes in a fighter's stance.

stages.name: Roobrawler
stages.look: A muscular kangaroo boxer with a gold champion belt and a taped tail. A tiny joey with miniature gloves peeks out of its pouch, copying every move.

dex: It trains its joey from the pouch, one jab at a time. Forgewall's arena keeps a belt that only a Roobrawler has ever held.

why: Dragon has only 5 catchable families and has never been paired with Ground. This is the set's pseudo-legendary: three stages, a slow climb to 52 and the highest total in the set as the reward.

stages.name: Burrowyrm
stages.look: A legless young sand-wyrm peeking out of its burrow, with a spade-shaped snout for digging, small horn nubs and bright curious eyes.

stages.name: Dunescale
stages.look: A young sand-dragon that has grown short, powerful legs. Its back is covered in thick sandstone plates, its spade snout has hardened into a digging horn, and stubby frills flare when it is angry.

stages.name: Mesadrake
stages.look: A heavy, low four-legged desert dragon built like a giant monitor lizard, wide and long rather than tall. Its back carries three flat-topped red rock plateaus like a row of mesas, with violet scales showing between them. A broad spade-shaped head with two short horns, a thick dragging tail and a small swirl of sand around its claws. Calm, ancient expression.

dex: The red mesas of Deepcut are said to be the backs of sleeping Mesadrakes. When one stretches, a new canyon opens.
